lines.name: North Pacific Coast, Sausalito to the Russian River
lines.summary: A narrow-gauge railroad from the ferry at Sausalito over White's Hill to Point Reyes, around Tomales Bay to Tomales, and through the redwoods to the Russian River at Duncans Mills (1877), later Cazadero (1886).
lines.fate_note: Trains between Point Reyes and Monte Rio ended on April 3, 1930 (CRC Decision No. 22672), and between Manor and Point Reyes on August 1, 1933, replaced by Pacific Greyhound's stages (Decision No. 34457).

route.note: Drawn to April 3, 1930, when the narrow gauge to Monte Rio ceased: the line's trains could reach this stretch only over it. When they last ran beyond Monte Rio isn't sourced.

sources.note: Opened for public use from Sausalito to Tomales on January 11, 1875, Tomales to Howards October 16, 1876, Howards to Tyrone April 2, 1877, Tyrone to Duncans May 15, 1877 (p. 154), and "Duncans to Cazadero April 11, 1886" (p. 18).

"The formal opening of the North Pacific Coast Railroad took place on Thursday, January 7, 1875 … from Saucelito to Tomales" (p. 333); the route by Fairfax, White Hill and San Geronimo creek (pp. 147-148).
The first passenger train reached Occidental (Howard's) "October 16, 1876".
"Saucelito, Cal., to Duncan's Mills, Cal 74.25 miles"; three-foot gauge.
"Main Line — San Francisco to Cazadero, Cal. (ferry, 6 m.; RR., 80.75 m.)".
The narrow gauge "between Point Reyes and Monte Rio": "operation thereof ceased on April 3, 1930".
"Prior to August 1, 1933 service … [was] performed by steam train. On that date … applicant discontinued operations between Point Reyes and Manor."
The order of January 9, 1933 authorizing the end of passenger and mixed trains between Manor and Point Reyes, once Pacific Greyhound's stages ran.
The North Shore Railroad's track between Sausalito and San Rafael, electrified in 1903.

lines.notes: Drawn as its own line over the track it shared with the North Shore's electric trains from 1903 (decision 21). How far the trains to Point Reyes ran over the electrified track in later years isn't sourced; the map draws the line from Sausalito, as the North Pacific Coast built it, until its last trains in 1933. Not drawn: Sheridan to Duncans Mills and Cazadero, which no sheet of the line's years shows (a map to georeference by hand), and the tunnels at White's Hill and into Sonoma County. When the North Shore and then the Northwestern Pacific took it over isn't sourced here.

lines.name: North Pacific Coast San Rafael branch
lines.summary: The North Pacific Coast's two-mile branch from its main line at the Junction (San Anselmo) to San Rafael, where its passengers took the San Rafael & San Quentin to the ferry.

running.note: "The first shipment made over the road to San Francisco via San Rafael was on January 8, 1875".
"San Rafael Branch : Junction, Cal., to San Rafael, Cal 2.00 miles."
"San Rafael Branch … Junction, Cal., to San Rafael, Cal 2.00 m."

lines.notes: When the branch opened and when its steam trains gave way to the North Shore's electric line (1903) aren't sourced; it is drawn for the years the sources show it (decision 20). The track is the one the electric line used.

lines.name: San Rafael & San Quentin trains, Point San Quentin to San Rafael
lines.summary: Trains between the ferry wharf at Point San Quentin and San Rafael, first the San Rafael & San Quentin's own, then, under the North Pacific Coast's lease from 1875, the narrow gauge's: until 1884 San Quentin was its passenger terminal, with boats from San Francisco meeting trains for San Rafael, the Junction (San Anselmo) and the Russian River. Later a steam shuttle, which kept running after the lines to San Rafael were electrified in 1903.
lines.fate_note: Passenger service between San Rafael and San Quentin ended in 1913 (Western Railroader, 1949); the branch went on carrying freight.

route.note: In 1877-84 the boats' trains ran on over the San Rafael branch to the Junction (San Anselmo) and the main line.

sources.note: The first trip, March 21, 1870 (p. 333); "the San Quentin terminus is used principally for the passenger business" (p. 148).
The North Pacific Coast's lease, from March 11, 1875 to March 11, 1918.
Boats "for San Quentin, San Rafael, and Junction", connecting with trains.
"Trains marked * run to San Quentin" in the North Shore's timetable of 1903.
"The line extends to San Quentin … but this extension is not in operation at present."

Standard gauge, relaid to three-foot gauge in 1875 (p. 7); steam trains between San Rafael and San Quentin after 1903 (p. 7); "Passenger service was discontinued between San Rafael and San Quentin" in 1913 (p. 10).

lines.notes: The end in 1913 rests on one railfan history (Borden, in the Western Railroader of 1949); no Railroad Commission order or newspaper for it was found, and its day isn't known. Poor's of 1885 and a 1939 railfan article give the opening as 1871; the ferry's advertisement of 1870 calls the railroad "recently constructed".

lines.name: San Quentin ferry, San Francisco to Point San Quentin

running.note: Minturn's steamer Contra Costa, with stages to San Rafael, before the railroad.
"Connecting at Point San Quentin with the recently constructed Railroad to San Rafael".
The North Pacific Coast's steamer San Rafael "between San Francisco and San Quentin (connecting with trains at latter place)".
Boats "For SAN RAFAEL (via San Quentin Ferry)".

lines.summary: Steamers from the Davis St wharf in San Francisco to Point San Quentin, at first Charles Minturn's, with stages and from 1870 the railroad to San Rafael; from 1875 the North Pacific Coast's boats, which met its passenger trains there until 1884.
lines.fate_note: The North Pacific Coast's timetable from April 27, 1884 sends every boat by Saucelito.

sources.note: The last advertisement found with the San Quentin ferry.
"Commencing Saturday, April 27th, 1884": no San Quentin ferry.

lines.notes: Closed in April 1884, with the timetable printed as beginning "Saturday, April 27th, 1884"; April 27 was a Sunday, so the day is uncertain. When the ferry began isn't sourced; it ran by April 1867.

lines.name: San Quentin branch freight, San Rafael to Point San Quentin

running.note: San Rafael 17.0 to San Quentin 20.1 miles, with no scheduled trains.
The last employee timetable found that lists the branch.

lines.summary: The San Quentin branch after its passenger trains ended in 1913: a freight branch of the Northwestern Pacific, in its employee timetables until 1933 (decision 15).
lines.fate_note: Gone from the timetable that took effect on January 15, 1934; when it was abandoned isn't sourced.

sources.note: The page that superseded p. 4 of No. 12 on January 15, 1934 has no San Quentin table.

lines.notes: Drawn as freight from the passenger trains' end in 1913 to its last timetable in 1933 (decisions 15 and 20); the freight before 1929 isn't otherwise shown.
